title: The Therabot will see you now.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Europe PMC core record for PMID 42462035: single author (Jacobson NC), one page (p. 253, vol 393 issue 6808), isOpenAccess=N, hasSuppl=N, hasData=N, no cross-references, no text-mined accessions, no PMCID so no full text. Ran paper_context.py (zero accessions, zero NCBI links, empty repository search). Searched Zenodo (7 unrelated hits, none from this paper or the Dartmouth group) and Dryad (0 hits) for 'therabot'. The Science DOI page returns HTTP 403 to automated fetch.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: The one-sentence abstract ('Generative artificial intelligence can scale precision evidence-based psychotherapy') is all the text available. Everything about what the piece argues, and the 210-participant Therabot trial it refers to, comes from the journal's news release and secondary coverage, not from the article itself. I opened no data file because none is attached.

a1_downloadable.note: There is no dataset. This is a one-page, single-author Perspective/commentary in Science (p. 253) with no supplementary materials, no accessions and no repository deposit; Europe PMC flags hasSuppl=N and hasData=N, and Zenodo/Dryad searches returned nothing belonging to this work. The clinical data it discusses (the 210-participant Therabot randomized trial, Heinz et al., NEJM AI 2025) is identifiable human psychotherapy-session and symptom-scale data that was not released publicly.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: No files exist, so no label column exists. Any target (e.g. symptom-score change) would have to be obtained from a trial team under a data-use agreement.

a3_inputs_present.note: No inputs of any kind are distributed; chatbot conversation transcripts are not shared.

a4_units_stated.note: Not applicable: no data table to carry units.

a5_enough_rows.note: No rows available. Even the underlying trial reported N=210 participants, far under the ~1,500-row bar, and that count comes from secondary coverage rather than a file I opened.

a6_fits_laptop.note: Trivially passes only because there is nothing to download.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: No download exists to compare against any stated count.

a8_label_provenance.note: Cannot be traced: no label, no file, no codebook. The commentary itself reports no new measurements.

honest_claim_h3: No claim is possible: the article is an opinion piece with no accompanying data, so nothing can be modelled or evaluated from it.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use therapy chat messages to predict which patients' depression and anxiety scores improve during AI-delivered talk therapy.
plain_idea.train_on: What a model would need is each trial participant's conversation turns with the chatbot plus their baseline questionnaire scores; the number of examples is at most 210 participants, and none of it is downloadable.
plain_idea.predict: Change in standard symptom questionnaires (for example the PHQ-9 depression scale and GAD-7 anxiety scale, both self-report instruments) from before to after four weeks of chatbot use, as measured in the original randomized trial.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Clinicians and digital-health regulators would want to know in advance who benefits from an AI therapist and who needs a human; but the idea cannot be attempted here because neither the transcripts nor the scores are public.

ml_idea: Nothing actionable. The only project this piece suggests — predicting individual response to a generative-AI psychotherapy chatbot from conversation content — requires the Dartmouth Therabot trial's transcripts and symptom scores, which are identifiable human-subjects data and are not deposited anywhere. Chase the primary trial paper or a public mental-health conversation corpus instead, not this commentary.

effort.compute_note: No estimate possible and none needed: there are no files to load. Nothing was timed.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Read the Europe PMC record's hasSuppl/hasData flags and the page range — one page, single author, no supplement means it is a Perspective with no data. That took one call.

verdict_reason: One-page single-author Science Perspective with no data, no supplement, no accessions; A1 fails outright.
